gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.
What the light-blue bar at the right edge of the port side is. The guide's text and its callouts do not name it; the chassis ID lamp is on the rear.

The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin because the tongue colour follows the photograph (qfx5120-48y-rear-high.jpg), which shows a black tongue, not the blue of a USB 3.0 port.
The vertical rating label at the right edge of the rear (an AC input line, a DC input line and a line about each power supply). It is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.
The colour and blink pattern of the fan slot lamps beyond the guide's Table 24 (green and amber).

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 9: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.09 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52.02 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 23.7 lb (10.75 kg) with two supplies and the fans. The width is the body: the table says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend it to 19 in, so the brackets are not part of the body and are not modelled. Table 9 gives the 48T, 48Y and 48YM one set of figures.

colour.note: The front plate samples #8a8e97 (median of three bare patches) and the rear panel about #78787c; the fan strips and chassis rear read #929296. The chassis colour is the front's. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide lists the rack mount kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (shipped with the switch; also sold as EX-4PST-RMK) and describes flush, recessed and two-post mounting with the brackets; the library holds no kit contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-blue-bar.note: A light-blue bar stands at the right edge, 1.8 mm wide, between 12.6 and 33.4 mm down. The guide's text does not name it; it is drawn as decor and recorded as a gap. The photographed unit is the front-to-back build.

gate-1.note: The front studio photograph is orthographic enough to measure: its body, between the left rim and the right edge, is 1888 px wide and 187 px high, an aspect of 10.04 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09 (0.5 percent out, inside a pixel of edge placement). Scale 4.282 px/mm across, and the same down. The rear photograph reads 1880 x 186, 10.1, at 4.264 px/mm. The guide's own figure 30 is a half-tone thumbnail and is used only to count and to read the printing.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide states none. Third-party trackers (router-switch.com, serviceexpress.com) list an announcement of 2021-01-20 and end of sale of 2021-10-04 for the earlier QFX5120-48Y-AFO, -AFI, -DC-AFO and -DC-AFI part numbers, not for the -AFO2 and -AFI2 numbers this guide lists, so the device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

mgmt-labels.note: The upper management jack is printed C0 above it and the lower C1 below it on this device. The guide's callouts say C1 for item 3 and C0 for item 9 without saying which is on top; the photograph settles it. The QFX5120-48YM prints them the other way up.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX5110-FANAFO and -FANAFI) and the power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AO and -AI) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay: the supplies' own fans are inside the supplies. The guide's Table 23 names the fan part numbers and Table 25 the supply part numbers.

port-lamps.note: DRAWING AND PHOTOGRAPH DISAGREE, and the lamps are carried from the drawing. Guide figure 32 draws a small ring either side of every SFP28 numeral and four rings along each QSFP28 cage; the studio photograph shows none (the lamps are unlit light pipes and do not resolve at its scale), and a control confirms it: the numerals the rings sit beside resolve at the same scale. Table 18 states two lamps for each SFP28 port, link activity and status, and Table 19 four for each QSFP28 port, the first for the unchannelized link and the other three for channels. The lamp offsets from the numeral (3.0 mm either side for SFP28; 4.1 mm apart for QSFP28) are read off figure 32 at 6.3 px/mm and are estimated. Figure 54 captions the QSFP28 lamps as those of the top row, while figure 32 draws them in both rows; both rows are drawn, following the table's four lamps per port.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph: the SFP28 ports run 0 to 47 down each column, even above the cage and odd below it, the numeral printed on a line above the upper row and another below the lower row, one beside each lamp pair; the QSFP28 ports are 48 and 49 down the first column, 50 and 51, 52 and 53, 54 and 55, printed at the left of each cage. The guide's figure 32 prints the same numerals. Interface names are not printed and the guide held does not state them; none is written here.

ports.note: Front photograph, dark cage openings along the upper row: 24 columns of 13.78 mm openings on a 14.24 mm pitch, which is the registry's 14.25 SFP28 pitch to 0.01 mm, in three groups of eight with gutters of 2.5 and 2.55 mm (the openings start at 7.71, 124.24 and 240.78 mm, so the cells start at 7.5, 124.05 and 240.6). Then four QSFP28 openings 18.68 mm wide at 358.24, 377.39, 396.31 and 415.46, a 19.07 mm pitch against the registry's 19.0, which is used. Counts are 48 and 8, the guide's callouts 1 and 2 of figure 32.

power.note: Table 29 (AC supplies, QFX5120-48Y): 155 W typical, 283 W maximum, input 100 to 240 VAC at 6 A. Table 39 (DC supplies): 319 W typical and 342 W maximum, 10.5 A, rated -48 to 60 VDC. The two tables carry different figures for the same box and the guide states no ambient or scope for either, so both are kept and the AC pair is filed as the device's, since AC is the default build. The guide's maximum-power note about 3.5 W optics is printed under the 32C only.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.264 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 31 and callouts 1 to 12 of figure 33. At the left a 63.4 mm panel carries the four chassis lamps, the RJ-45 console jack with the USB port beneath it in one shield, the two stacked RJ-45 management jacks, the ESD point and the reset pinhole; then five fan slots numbered 0 to 4 on a 49.0 mm pitch, each preceded by a strip with its fan symbol, number and lamp; then the two supply slots 0 and 1, each preceded by a strip with its power symbol and number, and at the right edge a dark strip carrying a vertical rating label. The orange fan faces measure 40.8 to 41.0 mm wide and 41.5 mm high.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The guide's figure 33 draws the fan slots with AIR IN labels (a back-to-front unit); the studio photograph shows AIR OUT with orange (Juniper Gold) handles. The photograph is the front-to-back build, which is the default configuration here. Table 7 (the fan airflow table) and Table 26 settle the labels: AIR OUT with Gold handles for front-to-back, AIR IN with Azure Blue handles for back-to-front.

row-pitch.note: Down the first SFP column the two openings are 10.98 to 19.15 and 24.99 to 33.16 mm, centres 15.07 and 29.07, 14.0 apart; down the first QSFP28 column 11.44 to 19.85 and 24.52 to 32.93, centres 15.65 and 28.7, 13.05 apart. THE REGISTRY'S 15.0 SFP ROW PITCH IS MEASURED ON A DIFFERENT CAGE and is not a conformance figure, so the photograph's 14.0 is used; the 10.4 mm cell fits it without overlap. The y origin of the photograph is its top edge at 151 px, so each y is as accurate as that edge to about 0.25 mm.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5120 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-09-30, 339 pages (copyright HPE): the front and rear figures 30 to 34, Table 7 (models and variants), Table 9 (physical specifications), the LED sections (Tables 11, 13, 18, 19, 24, 34), the airflow tables 23 and 26 and the power tables 29 and 39. Juniper's studio photographs of the 48Y, front and rear, 2100 x 541 and 2100 x 567 px (image library, qfx5120-48y-front-high and -rear-high). THE HPE DATASHEET (a00150810enw) DID NOT ANSWER, a transport error on the one attempt, so no datasheet figure is used; every figure here is the guide's or is read off a photograph. No mechanical drawing and no 3D model were found.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the light latch tongues at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention, here read off the device for the SFP rows. The QSFP28 pairs show the same.

vents.note: The photograph shows two staggered rows of round holes along the top edge (centres about 3.3 and 5.1 mm down) and two along the bottom (about 40.1 and 41.9 mm), 3.2 mm apart along a row, which agrees with the guide's figure 32; drawn as two vent strips on a 3.2 by 1.85 mm pitch. The vertical profile through one column (holes at 3.0 to 4.7 and 39.2 to 40.9 mm) sees only one row of the stagger, which is why the pitch is read across the strip and not down one column.
